not_proved: Which residual ledgers survive global G-equivariance and landing
A numerical common plane order m for an actual covariant

statements.claim: For a homogeneous G-covariant p of degree d: if d even then p|_{E_-(t)}=0; if d odd then p|_{E_-} is an ordinary binary D12-covariant E_-→E_- (or zero).
If the common plus-plane order is the odd integer m and the odd restriction is nonzero, then p|_{E_-} = Δ_t^m h_t with h_t det-twisted of degree d−6m.
The ordinary and det-twisted binary covariant modules are free of rank 2 over R=Q[xy, x^6+y^6], generated in degrees 1 and 5.  Hilbert series (t+t^5)/((1-t^2)(1-t^6)).  This controls ALL degrees.

For residual degree e=1 or 3: only swap_both.  For e=5: three ledgers (not preserve_both).  For e≥7 odd: all four ledgers occur in the local D12 module.  Centralizer symmetry alone does not force a unique global transition.
The four local endpoint ledgers are not claimed to extend to global G-covariants; global restriction maps may cut the module.

ordinary_module_O.verification_of_freeness: dim O_{2k+1} = floor((2k+3)/3).  The free module R·g1 ⊕ R·g5 has Hilbert series (t + t^5)/((1-t^2)(1-t^6)).  Expanding: 1/((1-t^2)(1-t^6)) = sum_{a,b≥0} t^{2a+6b}; times t gives degrees 1+2a+6b; times t^5 gives 5+2a+6b.  For odd d=2k+1 the number of representations equals floor((d+2)/3).  Checked computationally for d≤60 in the verifier.
